final_recommendation: The room converged on a bilateral labor protocol (Mexico-U.S. only) with facility-level inspections, binding panel findings, and a 15-day post-finding tariff trigger. Protocol language was locked with exact terms demanded by labor and Congress. The final barrier is scheduling a floor vote by end of week to preserve business confidence.
minority_objections: Mexico initially resisted automatic tariff triggers as economic coercion, insisting on dispute-resolution remedies instead of pre-set consequences
U.S. Congress initially demanded tariffs trigger on inspection delays (not panel findings), which Mexico rejected as sovereignty infringement
key_conflicts: Automatic tariff trigger timing: Congress wanted tariffs on inspection delays; Mexico insisted on panel-based process to preserve sovereignty
Enforcement mechanism credibility: Labor/Congress demanded concrete facility access and binding consequences vs. Mexico's concern about U.S.-imposed remedies
Timeline pressure: Business lobby demanded floor vote date by end of week vs. Congress needing to validate protocol language with caucus first
key_concessions: Mexico accepted facility-level inspections and binding independent panels (conceding sovereignty concerns in exchange for due process)
U.S. Congress shifted from delay-based tariff trigger to post-finding trigger (accepting Mexico's due-process framing)
Canada stayed out of labor protocol negotiations, preserving dairy terms and Chapter 19 in exchange for bilateral scope
Mexico committed to same-day enforcement of protocol upon signature
red_lines: Canada: dairy concessions and Chapter 19 not reopened (would only accept bilateral Mexico-U.S. labor protocol)
Mexico: no automatic tariffs on inspection delays; remedies must follow panel findings, not timers
U.S. Congress/Labor: protocol must contain exact terms 'facility-level inspections' and 'binding panel finding' or no vote
Business lobby: floor vote must be scheduled by end of week or investor confidence craters
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Implementation capacity: no discussion of whether Mexico's labor inspectorate can actually execute facility-level inspections at scale
Political sustainability in Mexico: no assessment of domestic Mexican political backlash to U.S.-driven labor enforcement
Canadian ratification risk: assumed Canada would ratify amended package without testing Canadian parliamentary appetite
Enforcement precedent: no discussion of whether rapid-response mechanism sets template for future trade agreements or other sectors
downstream_risk_variables: Congressional leadership willingness to schedule floor vote by end of week
Democratic caucus acceptance of protocol language once reviewed in detail
Business community confidence if vote slips past the end-of-week deadline
Mexico's actual implementation of facility-level inspections post-ratification
Canadian parliamentary ratification of amended USMCA package
Media narrative momentum if vote timing slips
uncertainty_notes: Protocol language is locked and all parties claim alignment, but actual floor vote scheduling remains uncertain. Business lobby set hard deadline (end of week) for vote date or investor confidence collapses. No confirmation that Congressional leadership has committed to that timeline. Also unclear whether Canadian ratification is genuinely assured or merely assumed.

marker_evidence.ratification_risk: Drove entire meeting: 'My members won't vote yes on that' (R1), '218 votes' repeated, protocol amendment required to unlock ratification
marker_evidence.labor_enforcement_pressure: Central driver: facility-level inspections, binding panels, automatic tariff triggers dominated all three rounds; union threatened to 'walk' without exact language
marker_evidence.business_lobby_support: Genuine consideration but not dominant: lobby conditioned support on vote timing/certainty ('end of week or boards bail'), but deferred to labor/Congress on substance
marker_evidence.canadian_domestic_acceptability: Mentioned briefly: Canada insisted dairy/Ch19 off table if bilateral protocol, then stayed silent; not developed as driving concern
marker_evidence.mexico_labor_sovereignty_risk: Developed theme: Mexico resisted automatic tariffs as 'economic coercion,' insisted on panel process, but ultimately accepted binding findings—shaped compromise structure
marker_evidence.media_public_pressure: Developed consideration: media actor framed narrative pressure ('labor wins facility access' vs 'Congress stalls'), influenced urgency but didn't drive substance
marker_evidence.agreement_stability: Central driver: entire room treated ratification as contingent on protocol amendment; 'deal dies' language if amendment fails or vote timing slips
